source_text: Ἡμεῖς δὲ μετὰ τὸ οὕτως λοῦσαι τὸν πεπεισμένον καὶ συγκατατεθειμένον ἐπὶ τοὺς λεγομένους ἀδελφοὺς ἄγομεν, ἔνθα συνηγμένοι εἰσί, κοινὰς εὐχὰς ποιησόμενοι ὑπέρ τε ἑαυτῶν καὶ τοῦ φωτισθέντος καὶ ἄλλων πανταχοῦ πάντων εὐτόνως, ὅπως καταξιωθῶμεν τὰ ἀληθῆ μαθόντες καὶ δι᾿ ἔργων ἀγαθοὶ πολιτευταὶ καὶ φύλακες τῶν ἐντεταλμένων εὑρεθῆναι, ὅπως τὴν αἰώνιον σωτηρίαν σωθῶμεν. Ἀλλήλους φιλήματι ἀσπαζόμεθα παυσάμενοι τῶν εὐχῶν. Ἔπειτα προσφέρεται τῷ προεστῶτι τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἄρτος καὶ ποτήριον ὕδατος καὶ κράματος, καὶ οὗτος λαβὼν αἶνον καὶ δόξαν τῷ πατρὶ τῶν ὅλων διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου ἀναπέμπει καὶ εὐχαριστίαν ὑπὲρ τοῦ κατηξιῶσθαι τούτων παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πολὺ ποιεῖται· οὗ συντελέσαντος τὰς εὐχὰς καὶ τὴν εὐχαριστίαν πᾶς ὁ παρὼν λαὸς ἐπευφημεῖ λέγων· Ἀμήν. Τὸ δὲ ἀμὴν τῇ ἑβραΐδι φωνῇ τὸ γένοιτο σημαίνει. Εὐχαριστήσαντος δὲ τοῦ προεστῶτος καὶ ἐπευφημήσαντος παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ οἱ καλούμενοι παρ᾿ ἡμῖν διάκονοι διδόασιν ἑκάστῳ τῶν παρόντων μεταλαβεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ εὐχαριστηθέντος ἄρτου καὶ οἴνου καὶ ὕδατος καὶ τοῖς οὐ παροῦσιν ἀποφέρουσι.
pass_a_gloss: We, after having washed thus the one who has been convinced and has assented to the so-called brothers, lead him where they are gathered, making common prayers on behalf of themselves and the one who has been enlightened and all others everywhere, so that having learned the true things we may be deemed worthy and be found to be good citizens through deeds and guardians of the things entrusted, so that we may be saved for eternal salvation. We greet one another with a kiss after stopping the prayers. Then bread and a cup of water and wine are offered to the one presiding over the brothers, and he, having taken praise and glory to the Father of all through the name of the Son and the Holy Spirit, sends it up and makes a thanksgiving for being deemed worthy of these things by him for a long time; when he has finished the prayers and the thanksgiving, all the present people shout, saying: Amen. The Amen in the Hebrew language means 'so be it'. After the presider has given thanks and all the people have shouted, the ones called deacons by us give to each of the present ones to partake of the bread and wine and water that have been given thanks for, and they carry it away to those who are not present.

choices.why: Hebrew word used in Christian worship

pass_b_english: After the person who has been convinced and has assented is washed in this way, we bring them to the so-called brothers, where they are gathered together, so that we may offer common prayers for ourselves, for the one who has been enlightened, and for all others everywhere. We pray so that, having learned the true things, we may be deemed worthy and be found to be good citizens through our deeds and guardians of the things entrusted to us, so that we may be saved for eternal salvation. We greet one another with a kiss after the prayers have ended.

Then bread, a cup of water, and wine are offered to the one presiding over the brothers. He takes them and offers praise and glory to the Father of all through the name of the Son and the Holy Spirit, and he makes a lengthy thanksgiving for having been deemed worthy of these gifts by him. When he has finished the prayers and the thanksgiving, all the people present shout out, saying: Amen. In the Hebrew language, Amen means "so be it." After the presider has given thanks and all the people have shouted, those we call deacons give each of those present a share of the bread, wine, and water over which thanks has been given, and they carry it to those who are absent.

review.notes: All clauses in the Greek source [p1] are accounted for in both Pass A and Pass B. Pass A is a more literal translation of the syntax, while Pass B is a smoother rendering, but both preserve the agency, modality, and doctrine of the original. The translation of 'φιλήματι' as 'kiss' and 'ἐπευφημῆσαντος' as 'shouted' is accurate to the context. Scripture citations are not present in the source text, so none are required.
